issues.description: Field SealSaloon.stock: The problem statement instructs students to create a final Stock field and initialize it in the instance constructor (i.e., instance initialization in constructor), but elsewhere in the same problem statement it explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances). The solution implements the field as a static final Stock initialized at declaration (private static final Stock stock = new Stock()). This contradiction (instance-final vs. static-final) will confuse students and can lead to attempted assignments to a static final field in a constructor, which is invalid in Java and causes compilation errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: state that SealSaloon.stock is a shared field and must be declared static final. Remove or update the sentence that says the stock should be initialized in the instance constructor. Clarify that the static final Stock may be initialized at declaration (e.g., private static final Stock stock = new Stock();) or in a static initializer block. Also keep the note that totalOrders should NOT be static so students understand the intended per-instance behavior.
